ca_patterson_left.blurb: Patterson Left is the tall, dome-like left half of Patterson Bluff, a remote granite cliff in the western Sierra foothills off Highway 168 between Shaver Lake and Courtright. The face rises well over a thousand feet, so most of the 17 routes are long, multi-pitch trad lines, with a handful of aid climbs and two sport lines. Free grades run from 5.9 into the 5.12s, with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12. It faces southwest and bakes in the sun, so cooler weather suits it best. Many parties walk to the top and rappel in rather than hike up from below, which gives the place a committed, out-of-the-way feel.

ca_pyramid_wall.blurb: Pyramid Wall is a southeast-facing cliff in the Rock Creek drainage of the Eastern Sierra, up around 9,500 feet above Mammoth Lakes. A big pyramid-shaped roof sits in the middle of the wall. The 17 routes are mostly bolted sport lines, plus several trad lines that want a small rack and two top-ropes. Difficulty sits almost entirely in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a single 5.9. The wall catches sun into mid-afternoon, though there are shady nooks where a belayer can wait out a hot day, and the high elevation makes it a good escape from valley heat.

ca_senior_wall.blurb: Senior Wall is a bolted crag tucked on the back side of Table Mountain, near Sonora in Tuolumne County. Almost every one of its 17 routes is sport, with a single easy trad line. Most of the climbing falls at 5.9 and 5.10, with a few 5.8s and one 5.11, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on moderate-to-intermediate grades. Routes range from vertical to slightly overhanging, and the style is physical and pumpy, with plenty of jugs and liebacks. Because it sits behind the main faces, it tends to be quieter than the front-side crags.

ca_voodoo_wall.blurb: Voodoo Wall is a south-facing wall at The Coven, in the Fawnskin area on the north shore of Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains. Its 17 routes are short, so you can fit in plenty of climbs in a visit. The mix is roughly half sport, a third trad and a few top-ropes, spanning 5.6 up to 5.11, with the largest share at 5.10. The base is a fairly flat ledge reached by scrambling up and left from the main Coven cliff. The wall is sunny through the morning and early afternoon, and cooler months give the best friction.

ca_transpire_wall.blurb: Transpire Wall is a granite roadside crag in Lee Vining Canyon along Tioga Road, around 8,700 feet in the Eastern Sierra. Most of its 17 routes are bolted sport lines, with a few trad lines that call for extra gear. Grades start at 5.10 and run up through 5.12, so it is a step-up crag for strong climbers rather than a beginner spot. With such a short walk from the car it works well for a quick session. The wall does not get sun until about 10 am, so mornings can be cold, and it offers good views.
ca_transpire_wall.parking_note: Park in the large dirt turnout on the left side of Tioga Road, a little under seven miles up from the Highway 395 and 120 junction in Lee Vining.
ca_transpire_wall.approach: Cross the road from the turnout and follow a loose, lightly worn use trail up to the wall. Sturdy shoes help on the loose dirt.

ca_opposite_main_wall.blurb: Opposite Main Wall is a sector of the Burney Limestone crag, known as the Shredding, about 26 miles east of Redding along Highway 299. It holds 17 climbs, mostly bolted sport routes plus a few top-ropes and boulder problems. Grades spread from low fifth class up to 5.12, and it has most of the easier routes at the crag, which makes it a good place for newer leaders. The wall stays shaded nearly all day and runs colder than the outer walls, so it is nicer on warm days. Expect some dirt and moss from light use, and watch for poison oak on the way in.
